name: return_gated_comparison_result
description: Returns 0 when a status word is zero; otherwise it calls another routine and returns 0 only if one stored value is below another and an indexed table entry equals 1, returning 1 in every other case.

name: fill_slots_and_locate_markers
description: Copies a pair of 32-bit values into each of 48 slots, clears one word and sets two words to -1, then scans two groups of eight table entries and records the index of each entry of kind 6 in one of two slots depending on whether its group matches a stored value.

name: record_flag_pass_result
description: Stores 1 in a status word when a byte flag is non-zero and 0 otherwise, clears a counter word, and calls another routine with the parameter; if the counter is still zero afterwards, the returned value is also stored in a second word, and that value is returned.

name: dispatch_four_subroutine_calls
description: Decompilation timed out, so only the recorded facts are known: the routine has 122 instructions, is called by two routines and calls four others.

name: evaluate_depth_stages_early_exit
description: Stores the current entry in a per-depth table and sets a stage code from 0 to 3 in a state record, running a sequence of checks over two sub-entries and a descending index loop that calls six other routines and returns early as soon as one reports success.

name: advance_depth_and_iterate_search
description: Advances the depth counter, stores the current entry and records a score, then repeatedly calls other routines, two of them through stored pointers, updating a stored value until a bound is reached, and returns a word from the global state or 1 at the bound.

name: push_pair_two_slots
description: When a byte flag is set and the level marker differs from the first value, it stores a pair of 32-bit values in the first of two slots, moving the old first slot into the second; if the second slot is occupied and another routine rejects the pair, it stores the pair in the second slot instead.

name: check_level_slots_for_match
description: When a stage word is non-zero, it tests the current level's record and then, unless a mode word is set or the stage equals 2, tests each of the two slots of the level, returning 1 on the first positive result and 0 otherwise.

name: update_maximum_if_within_bound
description: Returns 1 when the parameter does not exceed the first stored word of a record, and in that case raises a second stored word to the parameter if that word is currently lower; otherwise returns 0.

name: score_entry_and_update_bounds
description: Scores the current entry along one of two paths chosen by a mode word, storing results in per-depth slots and in the state record and calling several other routines; on one path it adds a value from 0 to 7 obtained through a stored-pointer call when a counter is zero, and it returns 0 or 1 depending on whether a bound was reached.

name: adjust_scores_by_threshold_category
description: At the first depth it grades two values returned by other routines into one of four categories using fixed thresholds and adds a quarter of a stored value times that category to two score words; at deeper levels it may zero a score word and return 1 when another routine returns more than 1.

name: copy_candidate_into_depth_slot
description: Calls another routine with the current level's record and copies the current candidate entry into the level's slot; at the first depth it also saves a stored value and, when the mode word is 5, replaces that value with another stored value.

name: try_codes_two_to_five
description: Marks the current depth's flag as set, then tries each code from 2 to 5 in turn by calling another routine and returns 1 as soon as one call succeeds; otherwise it clears the flag and returns 0.

name: scan_adjacent_candidates_for_entry
description: Records the given entry in the current depth slot with a fixed kind of 6, scans the positions around it and calls other routines on each qualifying position, then walks a stored entry list for the current index, calling another routine on each non-empty entry not of kind 6 and returning 1 at the first success.

name: enumerate_targets_by_kind
description: Stores the given entry and its kind in the current depth slot, then switches on the kind (1 to 6) to visit target positions computed from fixed offset tables, calling another routine on each free candidate and returning 1 as soon as one call reports success, otherwise 0.

name: try_two_offsets_from_table
description: Sets the current depth's flags, then for each pair of table-driven offsets stores the candidate, calls another routine on it and, when that succeeds, calls a second routine; it returns 1 as soon as both succeed for one pair and 0 if no pair succeeds.

name: try_midpoint_kind_six
description: When the previous level's entry is of kind 6 and another routine returns a value above 31, it sets this level's slot to kind 6 at the midpoint of the previous level's two stored values, then tries each neighboring value that passes an edge check, calling other routines on each and returning 1 on the first pair of successes.

name: unwind_depth_swap_indices
description: Saves the current depth, then steps back through each deeper level one at a time, swapping two index words and calling another routine on each level's slot; afterwards it lowers the depth by one and, when a flag is set, calls the routine once more on the slot.

name: replay_depth_slots_forward
description: Optionally calls a routine on the next slot when a flag is set, then steps the depth forward and, while it is below the saved depth, calls another routine on each slot in turn and swaps two index words after each call.

name: handle_jay_was_wrong_text
description: Refers to the text 'Jay was wrong #1' and makes four calls to other routines, one of them through a stored pointer, storing a result in a state word. When a mode word is set and the result is non-zero it either sets the state word to 1 or resets a counter, and otherwise calls a stored pointer with a fixed argument.

name: apply_move_update_board
description: A very long routine that works on square-indexed board positions: it compares start and end squares to derive a step count and direction, applies special cases by piece kind (3, 5 and 6), updates two stored piece records and makes many calls through stored pointers. The decompiled listing is cut off partway, so the description covers only the visible part.

name: initialize_two_handler_slots
description: Called through a pointer in data, it makes two calls to another routine with fixed record offsets, the constants 7 and 8, and a routine reference, and stores each returned value in its own state word.

name: run_two_routines_if_clear
description: When a state word is zero, it calls two other routines in sequence; otherwise it does nothing.

name: write_setup_words_for_channel
description: Calls another routine and, when a state word is non-zero, writes a fixed sequence of values to global words, choosing between two variants according to whether the high word of a parameter is zero; the sequence ends with one of two control words.

name: set_channel_one_sample_registers
description: Writes the sample address, length and period registers of channel 1 from a pointer-held record, along with interrupt and DMA control words, using one of two variants depending on whether a flag word is zero.

name: set_channel_zero_sample_registers
description: Writes the sample address, length and period registers of channel 0 from a pointer-held record, then writes the interrupt and DMA control words for that channel.

name: enable_channel_dma_by_parameter
description: Writes a channel-select word and its interrupt control word depending on whether the low word of the parameter is zero, then calls another routine with the value 2.

name: enable_channel_zero_dma
description: Writes the channel-zero select and interrupt control words and then calls another routine with the value 2.

name: reset_channel_control_twice
description: Writes a fixed set of channel control words, then calls a library routine twice, passing the values 8 and 7 together with two stored values from the state record.

name: set_record_status_advance
description: Sets a status word of the record to 256 and increments a counter in the state record; on the first call it also stores a value from the state record into the record and sets a timer field to 50, and on later calls it sets two other record fields to 256 and 2.

name: store_default_timer_value
description: Stores a value from the state record into a record field and sets the adjacent timer field to 50.

name: set_record_status_second_counter
description: Sets a status word of the record to 128 and increments a second counter in the state record; on the first call it also stores a value from the state record into the record and sets a timer field to 50, and on later calls it sets two other record fields to 128 and 1.

name: store_secondary_timer_value
description: Stores a value from the state record into a record field and sets the adjacent timer field to 50.

name: lookup_bounded_table_value
description: Returns 0 when a record's first value is 96 or more; otherwise it finds the first entry of a global table whose mask matches the record's second value, reads a word through a stored pointer indexed by the first value, and adds 224 to it when a flag bit in the record is set.

name: lookup_masked_table_value
description: Finds the first entry of a global table whose mask matches a record's second value, reads a word through a stored pointer indexed by a register value, and adds 224 to it when a flag bit in the record is set.

name: initialize_trackdisk_port_access
description: Refers to the texts 'ChessStuff', 'Jay's Disk Port', 'trackdisk.device' and the messages about failing to create a port and being unable to access the drive, and makes five calls to other routines. The decompilation timed out, so nothing more is known about its logic.

name: set_global_pair_clear_third
description: Copies the two 16-bit halves of its 32-bit parameter into two global words and clears a third global word.

name: store_long_clear_next_word
description: Stores its 32-bit parameter into a global variable and writes zero to a second global word.

name: process_length_in_512_pieces
description: Works through a length in pieces of up to 512 units, calling two other routines for each piece with running addresses held in global words, and handles any remainder last.

name: call_per_512_unit_piece
description: Decoded from a gap rather than a called path, it repeatedly calls another routine with a computed value while the length is positive, advancing a global word and the address by 512 units and a counter by one on each pass.

name: advance_512_unit_pieces
description: Loops while a length remains positive, calling another routine with a stored source value and destination value, then advancing a global word by 512, the destination by 512 and the source index by one, and reducing the length by 512 on each pass.

name: dispatch_pending_global_values
description: If a global word is zero and a second global value is non-zero, it calls two routines with no arguments and then two routines with a fixed constant and the second value; if the first global word is non-zero, it calls another routine with that word instead.

name: call_if_second_global_set
description: When a second global word is non-zero, it calls two routines with no arguments, then calls one routine with a fixed constant and another with the second global word as its value.

name: round_global_offset_512
description: Rounds a global offset up to the next 512-unit boundary, adds 2 to the computed value when a threshold is exceeded, and when the new value differs from the current offset calls other routines with the old and new values before storing the new offset.

name: issue_command_two_for_block
description: Writes command word 2 with its high bit set, the value 512, a second parameter and the first parameter shifted by nine bits into global words, then calls another routine to issue them.

name: issue_command_three_for_block
description: Writes command word 3 with its high bit set, the value 512, a second parameter and the first parameter shifted by nine bits into global words, then calls another routine to issue them.

name: retry_on_write_protected_message
description: Repeats a sequence of calls while a status word stays non-zero, passing the message 'Disk is write protected, try again.' to another routine on each retry, and then makes one more call before returning.

name: wrap_single_routine_call
description: Makes one call to another routine and returns; it does nothing else.

name: wait_for_battlechess_disk_insert
description: Refers to the text 'Insert the BattleChess disk.' It repeats while a status byte equals 29, passing the message to another routine and pausing for 300 units through a stored pointer after each prompt, and it stops once the status byte is zero.

name: issue_block_command_saved
description: Refers to the text 'Battle Chess'. It saves a 56-byte block from a fixed address to the stack, sets global words for a block command using the values 512 and 4096, and calls another routine; the saved block is copied back on every path, and the function returns 1 when that call returns zero, otherwise 0.

name: issue_saves_command_restore
description: Refers to the text 'ChessSaves'. It saves a 56-byte block, sets global words for a block command with a larger transfer value, calls another routine with a computed value and a fixed constant, then restores the block on every path and returns 1 when that call returns zero, otherwise 0.

name: store_global_copy_saved
description: Stores a global word in a base-relative slot, copies a 56-byte block from another base-relative location to a fixed address, calls another routine and returns 1.

name: restore_block_clear_status
description: Copies a 56-byte block from a base-relative location to a fixed address, clears a global word and returns 0.

name: store_global_copy_and_call
description: Stores a global word in a base-relative slot, copies a 56-byte block from another base-relative location to a fixed address, calls another routine and returns 1.

name: issue_command_four_for_block
description: Writes command word 4 with its high bit set into a global word and calls another routine with a fixed address.

name: reset_status_when_zero
description: When a global word is zero, it sets another global word to 9, clears the first one and calls another routine with a fixed address.

name: set_global_minus_one
description: Sets a global word to minus one and returns that value; the routine was decoded from a gap rather than a called path.

name: fill_stack_buffer_and_dispatch
description: Calls a stored-pointer routine with a fixed constant to fill a stack buffer, passes a second stack area and the parameter to another routine, writes the values 8 and 12 into the first two bytes of the buffer, then calls another routine with the buffer and a size of 32.

name: wait_for_chesssaves_disk_insert
description: Refers to the text 'Insert the ChessSaves disk.' It repeats while another routine's result is zero, passing the message on each prompt, and pauses for 300 units through a stored pointer after prompting.

name: pause_if_flag_set
description: If a word at a base-relative offset is non-zero, it pauses for 300 units through a stored pointer; otherwise it does nothing.

name: clear_global_word
description: Sets a global word to zero.

name: load_saved_game_list
description: Refers to the text 'No games saved.' It reads a 512-byte buffer and passes that message to another routine if the read fails; otherwise it fills eight record slots from the buffer, walks a list of entries of type 64 and calls routines for each, then clears one flag bit in every record slot.

name: run_load_selection_loop
description: Refers to the text 'Load'. It fills eight record slots from a buffer, then repeatedly makes library calls and loops over entries of type 64, calling routines on each selected entry until the selection ends, after which it clears a flag bit in every record slot.

name: continue_load_selection_loop
description: Re-enters the selection loop at a later point: it selects entries of type 64, calls routines on them, and moves to cleanup when a sentinel value of 9 is reached, then clears one flag bit in every record slot and returns.

name: finish_selection_entry_loop
description: Continues the selection loop, making the same library and routine calls for each entry, until the current entry's value is 9; it then makes a final call, clears one flag bit in every record slot and returns.

name: resume_selection_loop_at_sentinel
description: Resumes the selection loop by reselecting entries of type 64 and calling routines on each until the current value is 9, then clears one flag bit in every record slot. It keeps looping while the selected value is not -1.

name: resume_selection_loop_on_change
description: Repeats while the stored selection value differs from the current entry's value, reselecting entries of type 64 and calling routines on each; at the value 9 it finishes, and otherwise it runs the update step before clearing one flag bit in every record slot.

name: repeat_selection_until_value_stable
description: Repeats selection of entries of type 64, calling routines on each, until the current entry's value matches the stored value and a flag word is non-zero, then runs the update step and clears one flag bit in every record slot.

name: scan_selection_kind_64
description: Repeatedly selects entries while the current entry's type is 64, calling routines on each and treating the value 9 as the end of the list, then clears one flag bit in every record slot. It shares the update step used by the other entry points.

name: clear_selection_flags_after_update
description: Runs the update step: it calls routines, sets a stored value from an index-derived byte, and calls routines again when that value changes; it then clears one flag bit in each of eight record slots and returns.

name: run_save_name_entry_dialog
description: Refers to the text 'Save'. It runs a name-entry loop that accepts up to 14 typed characters, with backspace removing one and Return committing the name; it calls other routines to show the entered text and the selected record, and returns when the list's sentinel value of 9 is reached.

name: continue_name_entry_editing
description: Enters the name-entry loop at an inner point and handles keystrokes the same way, committing the name on Return and returning once the sentinel value of 9 is reached. The decompiled listing is cut off partway, so the description covers only the visible part.

name: handle_name_entry_keystroke
description: Enters the name-entry loop to process a single keystroke: backspace removes the last character, Return commits the name, and any other accepted key is appended up to 14 characters. The listing is cut off partway, so the description covers only the visible part.

name: reset_name_entry_and_resume
description: Clears the typed-character count and then runs the name-entry loop, which selects entries of type 64, calls routines on them and handles keystrokes until the sentinel value of 9 is reached.

name: append_name_character_and_resume
description: Entry point that appends one typed character to the name, limited to 14 characters, or commits the name when Return is pressed, then makes the closing display calls and returns.

name: restart_name_entry_loop
description: Re-enters the name-entry loop at its start, selecting entries of type 64 and handling keystrokes as usual, and returns when the sentinel value of 9 is reached. The decompiled listing is cut off partway, so the description covers only the visible part.

name: handle_typed_name_character
description: Enters the name-entry loop at the step that appends a typed character, capped at 14 characters, then continues the same keystroke loop. The decompiled listing is cut off partway, so the description covers only the visible part.

name: toggle_name_entry_cursor
description: Enters the name-entry loop at the cursor step, which replaces a vertical-bar cursor character with a space or the reverse when the name field is active, then continues the keystroke loop. The decompiled listing is cut off partway, so the description covers only the visible part.

name: show_name_entry_cursor
description: Enters the name-entry loop at the step that places a vertical-bar cursor at the current position, then continues the keystroke loop. The decompiled listing is cut off partway, so the description covers only the visible part.

name: clear_name_flag_and_resume
description: Clears the name-field active flag and then runs the name-entry loop, which selects entries of type 64, handles keystrokes and returns at the sentinel value of 9. The decompiled listing is cut off partway, so the description covers only the visible part.

name: select_name_slot_and_resume
description: Enters the name-entry loop at a step that switches the selected name slot, redraws the previous slot's text when the selection changes, and then continues the keystroke loop. The decompiled listing is cut off partway, so the description covers only the visible part.

name: finish_name_slot_update
description: Enters the name-entry loop at a step that terminates the current name field and redraws its text, then returns from the loop. The decompiled listing is cut off partway, so the description covers only the visible part.

name: run_name_loop_without_setup
description: Runs the name-entry loop from its top without first preparing a slot, selecting entries of type 64 and handling keystrokes until the sentinel value of 9 is reached. The decompiled listing is cut off partway, so the description covers only the visible part.

name: begin_editing_name_slot
description: Enters the name-entry loop at the step that makes the selected slot's name field active and displays its text, then continues the keystroke loop. The decompiled listing is cut off partway, so the description covers only the visible part.

name: clear_name_field_and_redraw
description: Enters the name-entry loop at a step that clears the typed name text when the active field has no characters, redraws the slot and continues the keystroke loop. The decompiled listing is cut off partway, so the description covers only the visible part.

name: switch_name_slot_selection
description: Enters the name-entry loop at a step that selects a different name slot, redraws the previously edited slot and continues the keystroke loop. The decompiled listing is cut off partway, so the description covers only the visible part.

name: dispatch_name_entry_key_code
description: Takes a key code from a register and handles it inside the name-entry loop: backspace removes a character, Return commits the name, and other accepted keys are appended up to 14 characters. The decompiled listing is cut off partway, so the description covers only the visible part.

name: close_name_entry_on_key
description: Enters the name-entry loop at its closing step, which commits or abandons the current name field and returns when the sentinel value of 9 is reached. The decompiled listing is cut off partway, so the description covers only the visible part.

name: delegate_to_single_routine
description: Makes one call to another routine and returns; it does nothing else.

name: copy_text_and_append_space
description: Fills the buffer at the first parameter using a fixed constant through a stored pointer, copies the text from the second parameter into it, measures the resulting length and writes a space after the last character, returning that length.

name: check_printable_character
description: Returns 1 when the low word of the parameter is between 32 and 126 inclusive, and 0 otherwise.

name: build_compacted_slot_table
description: Fills a table of eight 16-byte slots with zeros and marks the last byte of each slot as 255, then copies each active record from the list into the table in order, storing its index in the slot's last byte, and records the number of active records in a global word.

name: rebuild_compacted_slot_table
description: Clears an eight-slot table, marking the last byte of each slot as 255, then copies each active record into the table in order, storing its index in the slot's last byte and recording the active count in a global word.

name: copy_active_records_to_slots
description: Copies each active record from the list into consecutive slots in index order, storing the record's index in the slot's last byte, and records the number of copied slots in a global word.

name: draw_load_slot_list
description: Refers to the texts '---------' and 'Load'. It draws eight slot rows by calling library routines and other routines, then draws a count of up to nine at a computed position and a second line using a fixed constant and that count.

name: draw_load_panel_frame
description: Sets a display value and draws a frame and a second rectangle at fixed positions and sizes by calling library routines.

name: draw_optional_dialog_element
description: Sets a display value and draws two fixed elements, a third one only when the low word of the parameter is non-zero, and then one more fixed element, all through library routines.

name: draw_cancel_and_done_labels
description: Refers to the texts 'Cancel' and 'Done'. It draws a background element and a fixed-size element, adds a further element when the low word of the parameter is non-zero, then draws another element that uses a stored value of six bytes.

name: draw_rectangle_outline_from_corners
description: Builds five corner points of a rectangle from four values in an array, moves to the first corner through a library call and draws the outline through another routine.

name: open_window_or_report_error
description: Refers to the text 'unable to open a window.' It copies a stored value, opens a window through a library call using a rectangle in the state record, saves the returned handle, and passes the message to another routine when the handle is zero; it returns whether a handle was obtained.

name: return_constant_one
description: Returns the value 1 and does nothing else.

name: close_window_handle_if_open
description: If a stored window handle is non-zero, it closes it through a library call, makes a second library call with fixed values, clears the stored handle, and then calls another routine.

name: copy_block_or_clear
description: Fills a 32-byte stack buffer through another routine, then obtains a handle from another routine using the constant 1005; if the handle is non-zero it copies 512 bytes from it into the parameter and releases it, otherwise it clears the parameter block with a fixed flag value. It returns whether a handle was obtained.

name: run_two_calls_return_one
description: Makes one library call and one other routine call, then returns 1.

name: load_second_handle_block
description: Fills a 32-byte stack buffer through another routine, runs another routine when a state word is zero, then obtains a handle using the constant 1006; if the handle is non-zero it copies 512 bytes from it into the parameter and releases it. It returns whether a handle was obtained.

name: call_pair_and_return_one
description: Makes two calls to other routines and returns 1.

name: reset_saves_label_and_refresh
description: Refers to the texts 'ChessSaves' and 'ChessSaves:'. It clears the first byte of its buffer and, when a state word is zero, passes a global address to two routines before passing it to another routine once more.

name: fill_record_and_dispatch
description: Zeroes the first two words of a record, sets one byte to 2 and another to 0, stores the base register value and the third parameter at fixed offsets, then passes the record and the second parameter to another routine.

name: initialize_serial_port_registers
description: Obtains a value from another routine using the constant 11, stores it with two buffer addresses in state words, then writes interrupt control and serial period words to the global hardware words.

name: send_bytes_over_serial
description: Sends a counted run of bytes one at a time: it waits until the transmit-ready bit in the serial status word is set, then writes each byte with its ninth bit set, advancing through the buffer until the count reaches zero.

name: send_serial_bytes_wait
description: Writes a counted run of bytes to the serial data word with its ninth bit set, and waits for the transmit-ready bit in the status word between writes until the count reaches zero.

name: return_immediately
description: Returns without doing anything.

name: read_serial_ring_buffer_bytes
description: Copies bytes out of a ring buffer one at a time into the destination, polling another routine with a timeout of eight units while the buffer is empty; it returns zero when the requested count has been read and negative one when the timeout expires.

name: read_serial_bytes_at_loop
description: Re-enters the serial receive loop partway through: it stores each byte from the ring buffer into the destination, polling with a timeout, and returns zero when the count is exhausted or negative one on timeout.

name: return_negative_one
description: Returns the constant minus one to the caller.

name: read_serial_bytes_with_timeout
description: Reads bytes from the receive ring buffer into a destination, polling with a timeout of eight units for each byte, and returns zero when the requested count is reached or negative one when a timeout expires.

name: return_zero
description: Returns zero to the caller.

name: flush_serial_receive_buffer
description: Sets the receive buffer's read position equal to its write position, discarding any bytes that were waiting.

name: count_pending_serial_bytes
description: Returns the number of bytes waiting in the 128-byte receive ring buffer, computed as the write position minus the read position with wraparound.

name: compute_serial_offset_from_read
description: Computes the distance of a stack-held position from the receive read position, adding 128 when the result wraps around, and returns it as a word.

name: disable_serial_transmit_interrupt
description: Disables the serial transmit interrupt by writing its bit without the set flag, then calls another routine with the constant 11 and a stored value.

name: queue_serial_transmit_byte
description: Stores a byte into the 128-byte transmit ring buffer at the write position, wrapping back to the start at the end of the buffer, and sets a state word to 2048.

name: send_checksum_packet_retry
description: Builds a two-slot checksum over the packet body and sends the packet through another routine, then reads replies with a timeout: a timeout clears the first packet byte, a reply of -92 resends the packet, a reply of -91 ends the exchange, and any other reply reports an error; it gives up after five attempts.

name: resend_checksummed_packet_loop
description: Adds the packet body into a two-slot checksum, sends the packet through another routine and handles replies the same way as the neighbouring routine: -92 resends, -91 finishes, other values report an error, and it gives up after five attempts.

name: wait_for_reply_with_retries
description: Handles incoming reply bytes: a reply of -92 is answered, a reply of -91 ends the exchange, a timeout clears the first byte, and after five attempts it passes an error message to another routine.

name: poll_replies_with_collision_message
description: Refers to the text 'Sending at the same time...try again'. It polls for replies through another routine with a timeout, answers a reply of -92, ends on -91, and after five attempts or an unexpected reply it reports the error through another routine.

name: poll_replies_for_opponent_timeout
description: Refers to the text 'Opponent not responding'. It polls replies up to five times, clearing the first byte on a timeout and answering a reply of -92, and reports an error through another routine when attempts run out or an unexpected reply arrives.

name: parse_incoming_packet
description: Parses an incoming packet: a first byte whose top four bits equal 10 introduces a header whose length must be below 40 and whose body is checked against a fixed pattern, with type 166 sending a response and type 170 setting a flag. Bytes below 128 are read as a text line ending at a carriage return, and the routine returns zero when another routine reports a handled result, otherwise minus one.

name: dispatch_received_packet_with_reply
description: Checks a received packet's checksum against its trailer and then either sends a reply chosen by packet type 166 or sets a flag for type 170. Header bytes and text lines below 128 are handled as separate cases, and the routine returns zero when a packet is refused and minus one when no further input arrives.

name: exchange_packets_while_type_170
description: Repeats packet reception, validating checksums and sending replies, for as long as the packet type is 170; it returns zero when a packet of another type arrives.

name: send_ack_then_receive_packets
description: Sends a reply chosen by a flag word, then receives packets with the same checksum and text handling, returning minus one when no input is ready.

name: send_reply_and_receive_loop
description: Sends a fixed reply and then repeats packet reception with checksum checks until a packet of type 166 arrives; it returns zero for an unexpected packet type and minus one when no input arrives.

name: return_zero_value
description: Returns zero to the caller without performing any other operation.

name: exchange_packets_type_166_170
description: Sends a reply for packet type 166 or sets a flag for type 170, then receives packets with checksum checks, returning zero for any other packet type and minus one when no input arrives.

name: receive_packets_until_other_type
description: Receives packets with checksum checks, sending a reply for type 166 and setting a flag for type 170, and repeats until a packet of another type arrives; it then returns zero, or minus one when no input arrives.

name: verify_packet_checksum_and_reply
description: Sends a reply, then receives packets and compares each checksum with its trailer, answering type 166 or setting a flag for type 170 when the checksum matches. It returns zero for any other packet type and minus one when no input arrives.

name: receive_checked_packets_until_end
description: Receives packets of up to 39 bytes and checks each checksum, answering type 166 or setting a flag for type 170 on a match. It returns zero for any other packet type and minus one when no input arrives.

name: dispatch_text_and_checked_packets
description: Handles text lines below 128 by reading them up to a carriage return, and packet headers by checking their checksums and answering type 166 or setting a flag for type 170. It returns zero for other packet types and minus one when no input arrives.

name: receive_lines_with_ate_check
description: Reads text lines and packets in turn, copying each received line up to a carriage return and comparing its first four bytes with the characters 'ATE' followed by a zero byte. Packet headers are handled as in the neighbouring routines, and it returns minus one when no input arrives.

name: poll_packet_exchange_flag
description: Sets a state flag, then polls for packets and text lines: packet headers are checksummed and answered with type 166 or 170 replies, and text lines are compared with the characters 'ATE' followed by a zero byte. It returns zero for any other packet type and minus one when no input arrives.

name: send_status_packet_when_active
description: When either of two state words equals 2, it calls another routine with a 38-byte stack buffer and then sends a two-byte packet containing the values 161 and 37.

name: send_type_162_packet
description: Builds a four-byte packet of type 162 with length 6, copying the byte at offset 1 and the byte at offset 3 of its parameter, and sends it through another routine.

name: send_type_169_packet
description: Sends a two-byte packet of type 169 with length 5 through another routine.

name: send_fixed_quad_clear_state
description: Sends a fixed four-byte value through another routine and then clears a state byte to zero.

name: fill_buffer_with_descending_bytes
description: Writes a run of bytes into the destination buffer, each holding the low byte of a counter that counts down from the given count minus one to zero.

name: advance_seed_return_high
description: Calls another routine, adds 12345 to its result and stores the sum in a state longword, then returns the upper 15 bits of that longword as a word.

name: store_high_word_of_seed
description: Stores the upper 16 bits of its 32-bit parameter into a state word.

name: convert_lowercase_letter_to_uppercase
description: Converts the second byte of its parameter from lowercase to uppercase when it lies between 97 and 122 by subtracting 32, and returns any other byte unchanged. The routine was decoded from a gap rather than a called path.

name: convert_uppercase_letter_to_lowercase
description: Converts the second byte of its parameter from uppercase to lowercase when it lies between 65 and 90 by adding 32, and returns any other byte unchanged.

name: open_dos_library_or_alert
description: Refers to the text 'dos.library'. It zeroes 8524 longwords of global memory, stores the stack and exec base values, may call a supervisor routine, then opens a library; if the open call returns zero it calls the exec alert routine, otherwise it calls another routine.

name: no_operation_return
description: Returns immediately without doing anything.

name: allocate_and_initialize_port_block
description: Allocates a cleared block of six times a state word's length, sets its fields and writes the marker 'MANX' at its start, then calls other routines to set up its port and messages; if allocation fails it calls another routine with zeros.

name: tokenize_command_line_into_array
description: Splits a command line into tokens separated by spaces, tabs, form feeds, carriage returns and newlines, keeping double-quoted text together, copies each token into a buffer through a library call and records its address in a pointer array, which ends with a zero entry.

name: tokenize_command_line_for_caller
description: Performs the same command-line tokenizing as its neighbouring routine, splitting on whitespace and keeping quoted text together, then allocates a pointer array through another routine and fills it with the token addresses, ending with a zero entry.

name: copy_string_with_zero_padding
description: Copies bytes from a source string into a destination buffer until the count is exhausted or a null byte is copied, then writes zeros over the rest of the count, and returns the destination pointer.

name: copy_bounded_string_zero_padded
description: Copies bytes from a source string into a destination buffer until the count is exhausted or a null byte is copied, then fills the remaining bytes of the count with zeros, and returns the destination pointer.

name: copy_bytes_handling_overlap
description: Copies a counted run of bytes from a source to a destination, copying backwards when the destination lies above the source so overlapping regions are preserved, and does nothing when the two addresses are equal.

name: append_string_bounded
description: Appends a source string to the end of a destination string, copying up to a fixed large byte limit and terminating the result if the source was cut short, then returns the destination pointer.

name: append_string_with_length_limit
description: Appends a source string to the end of a destination string, copying no more than the count given in the third argument and writing a terminator if the copy was cut short, then returns the destination pointer.

name: compare_strings_with_limit
description: Compares two byte strings up to a fixed large limit, returning -1 when the first differing byte of the first string is smaller, 1 when it is larger, and 0 when the strings match through the terminator or the limit.

name: copy_string_to_buffer
description: Copies a null-terminated string from a source into a destination buffer, including the terminator, and returns the original destination pointer.

name: multiply_low_32_bits
description: Computes the low 32 bits of the product of two 32-bit register values from their 16-bit halves, returning that product in the first result register and the second input unchanged in the other.

name: locate_window_and_store_fields
description: Refers to the texts 'WINDOW' and 'icon.library'. It looks up data through library calls, and when a window record is found it stores two values from it in the parameter record, then releases the handle through a library call and clears the stored handle.

name: query_and_sum_library_values
description: Calls a library routine on a global with a flag of 1, makes further library calls to obtain a second value, adds the two results, stores the sum in an optional output parameter when one is given, and returns it.

name: query_timer_device_value
description: Refers to the texts 'timer is not available' and 'timer.device'. It opens the timer device through library calls, reports the failure through two library calls if opening fails, and otherwise reads a value from the device, adds a stored value and returns the sum, also storing it in an optional output parameter.

name: call_with_sign_corrected_result
description: Determines whether the signs of its two register inputs differ, calls another routine, negates that routine's result when they differ, and returns it in the first output register with the second input in the low register.

name: call_negate_if_first_negative
description: Calls another routine and returns its result, negated when the first input is negative, with the second input in the low register. The routine was decoded from a gap rather than a called path.

name: call_return_with_input_low
description: Calls another routine and returns its secondary result register as the high word, with the original second input register as the low word.

name: tail_call_other_routine
description: Calls another routine and returns without doing anything else.

name: divide_unsigned_32_bit_values
description: Divides a 32-bit unsigned dividend from one register by the divisor in another register: when the divisor's high word is non-zero it uses a 16-step shift-and-subtract loop, otherwise it divides in two steps by the low word, and it returns the quotient and remainder in a pair of result registers.

name: run_sixteen_step_divide_loop
description: Swaps the two halves of the second register and runs a 16-step shift-and-subtract loop against the first register, leaving the results in registers and returning no value.

name: measure_string_length
description: Returns the number of bytes in a zero-terminated string, not counting the terminator, without changing memory.

name: run_optional_handler_then_call
description: Calls a stored handler through a pointer when that pointer is set, then calls another routine and returns.

name: release_game_resources
description: Releases the resources held in the state record: it calls another routine for each of a count of entries, releases a block sized by a state word times six, invokes a stored handler pointer when set, and releases three further blocks whose fields are non-zero. When a flag bit is set it also calls the exec supervisor vector before returning a stored value.

name: release_game_resources_after_loop
description: Releases the same resources as its neighbouring routine, starting after the per-entry loop: it releases a block sized by a state word times six, runs stored handler pointers, releases three further blocks when their fields are non-zero, and calls the exec supervisor vector when a flag bit is set, then returns a stored value.

name: finish_resource_release
description: Releases the block described by two state fields when they are set, calling another routine to free it, and otherwise does nothing further, then returns a stored value.

name: call_twice_return_stored
description: Calls another routine, then calls it again with a stored handle, and returns a stored value.

name: return_from_gap_stub
description: Returns immediately without doing anything; the routine was decoded from a gap rather than a called path.

name: release_indexed_table_entry
description: Takes an index into a table of six-byte records; when the index is in range and the entry's first word is non-zero, it releases that entry through another routine unless a flag bit is set, clears the entry and returns 0. Otherwise it stores error code 2 and returns minus one.

name: release_entry_at_pointer
description: Releases the entry at its pointer parameter through another routine unless a flag bit in the entry is set, then zeroes the entry's first word and returns 0.

name: call_library_function_via_base
description: Calls a library function at a fixed offset from a library base stored in the state record. The decompiler could not recover the jump table, so the call target is unresolved.

name: close_dos_file_handle
description: Calls the DOS close function through the library base stored in the state record. The decompiler could not recover the jump table, so the call is treated as an indirect call.

name: call_dos_current_dir
description: Calls the DOS current-directory function through the library base stored in the state record. The decompiler could not recover the jump table, so the call is treated as an indirect call.

name: call_dos_delay
description: Calls the DOS delay function through the library base stored in the state record. The decompiler could not recover the jump table, so the call is treated as an indirect call.

name: call_dos_input
description: Calls the DOS Input function through the library base stored in the state record. The decompiler could not recover the jump table, so the call is treated as an indirect call.

name: call_dos_open_function
description: Calls the DOS Open function through the library base stored in the state record, with no arguments set up in this routine. The decompiler could not recover the jump table, so the call is treated as an indirect call.

name: call_dos_open_entry
description: Calls the DOS Open function through the library base stored in the state record. The decompiler could not recover the jump table, so the call is treated as an indirect call.

name: call_dos_output
description: Calls the DOS Output function through the library base stored in the state record. The decompiler could not recover the jump table, so the call is treated as an indirect call.

name: call_dos_read_handler
description: Calls the DOS Read function through the library base stored in the state record, as a handler reached from a data pointer. The decompiler could not recover the jump table, so the call is treated as an indirect call.

name: call_dos_read
description: Calls the DOS Read function through the library base stored in the state record. The decompiler could not recover the jump table, so the call is treated as an indirect call.

name: call_dos_seek
description: Calls the DOS Seek function through the library base stored in the state record. The decompiler could not recover the jump table, so the call is treated as an indirect call.

name: call_dos_write
description: Calls the DOS Write function through the library base stored in the state record and returns to its caller. The decompiler could not recover the jump table, so the call is treated as an indirect call.

name: call_dos_write_handler
description: Calls the DOS Write function through the library base stored in the state record, reached through a data pointer. The decompiler could not recover the jump table, so the call is treated as an indirect call.

name: call_second_library_entry
description: Calls the function at offset minus 108 from the library base held in the second state field and returns to its caller.

name: call_second_library_far_entry
description: Calls the function at offset minus 450 from the library base held in the second state field. The decompiler could not recover the jump table, so the call is treated as an indirect call.

name: call_second_library_mid_entry
description: Calls the function at offset minus 414 from the library base held in the second state field and returns to its caller. The routine was reached through a handler pointer.

name: call_second_library_mid_alt
description: Calls the function at offset minus 414 from the library base in the second state field, the same call as its neighbouring routine, and returns to its caller.

name: create_request_block_with_fields
description: Calls another routine with a fixed argument and, unless it returns -1, allocates a 34-byte cleared block through a library call; it stores the parameters, a fixed type byte and the returned value into the block and links it through another routine. It returns the block, or zero when the call returns -1 or allocation fails.

name: release_request_block_and_free
description: Releases a block created by its neighbouring routine: when its second word is set it calls another routine on the block, marks its fields as unused, calls another routine with the stored byte, and then frees the 34-byte block through a library call.

name: call_second_library_late_entry
description: Calls the function at offset minus 354 from the library base in the second state field. The decompiler could not recover the jump table, so the call is treated as an indirect call.
